title: Introduction to Node.js
description: Basics of Node.js including what it is, its history, key features, and why it's popular for backend development.

flashcards.question: What is Node.js?
flashcards.answer: Node.js is an open-source, cross-platform JavaScript runtime environment that allows running JavaScript code outside of a browser.

flashcards.question: Who created Node.js and when was it first released?
flashcards.answer: Node.js was created by Ryan Dahl and first released in 2009.

flashcards.question: What programming language does Node.js use?
flashcards.answer: Node.js uses JavaScript as its primary programming language.

flashcards.question: What is the main purpose of Node.js?
flashcards.answer: Node.js is mainly used to build fast, scalable backend and server-side applications.

flashcards.question: What is unique about Node.js’s architecture?
flashcards.answer: Node.js uses a single-threaded, event-driven, non-blocking I/O model that makes it efficient and suitable for I/O-heavy tasks.

flashcards.question: Why is Node.js considered good for real-time applications?
flashcards.answer: Because it handles many connections simultaneously with low latency thanks to its event-driven architecture.

flashcards.question: What is the V8 engine in Node.js?
flashcards.answer: V8 is Google’s open-source JavaScript engine that compiles JavaScript into native machine code, powering Node.js’s speed.

flashcards.question: Which company backs Node.js?
flashcards.answer: Node.js is maintained by the OpenJS Foundation, supported by companies like IBM, Microsoft, and Google.

flashcards.question: Name some common use cases for Node.js.
flashcards.answer: Web servers, APIs, real-time chat apps, streaming applications, and microservices.

flashcards.question: How does Node.js handle multiple requests?
flashcards.answer: Node.js handles multiple requests asynchronously using its event loop and non-blocking I/O operations.
